source: What a break from work costs in later pay: PayScale's 2018 career-gap research reported candidates with a year out of work earning in the region of 7% less than those without; Bertrand, Goldin and Katz (2010, American Economic Journal: Applied Economics) found MBA earnings fell markedly after career interruptions of six months or more; other studies find little or no penalty for short, planned breaks in fields with steady demand.
confidenceNote: Recalled figures from studies of different populations, none of them a planned micro-retirement of 1 to 12 months. The three bands are a convention chosen here to bracket them; the person can type their own figure and the room always shows the range.
note: Read by engines/microretirement.js (K5, D-219). penaltyPerYearOfBreak is the share of yearly pay given up, per year of break, for the rest of the working years; a six-month break at the middle band costs half of mid × pay × the years left.
